title: Height from homogeneous independence at a rational point
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a Noetherian commutative $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Let $\varepsilon:A\to k$ be a $k$-algebra homomorphism and put $I=\ker\varepsilon$. Let $\iota$ be a finite index set and choose $x_i\in I$ for $i\in\iota$. Suppose (i) every $a\in I$ can be written $a\equiv\sum_i c_i x_i\pmod{I^2}$ with $c_i\in k$, and (ii) for every integer $r\ge0$ and every homogeneous polynomial $f\in k[X_i:i\in\iota]$ of total degree $r$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $f(x)\in I^{r+1}$ implies $f=0$. Then $\operatorname{ht}(I)=\#\iota$, where height is the supremum of lengths of chains of primes contained in $I$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

proof.text: Apply AlgHom.homogeneous_independence_localization to R=A_I. It gives residue surjectivity from k, generation of the maximal ideal by the images of x_i, and the same homogeneous independence after localization.

Choose an equivalence of the finite index set with Fin n; renaming polynomials preserves homogeneity, evaluation and independence. Prove the local dimension equals n by induction. For n=0 the generated maximal ideal is zero, so the local ring is a field and has dimension zero.

For n+1 variables, homogeneous_independence_quotient makes x_0 a nonzerodivisor and gives homogeneous independence in A_I/(x_0). Surjectivity of the quotient map carries the maximal ideal to the maximal ideal. Its generating family is exactly the images of x_1,...,x_n, and residue representatives from k descend to the quotient.

Apply the induction hypothesis to the quotient, whose dimension is n. The nonzerodivisor dimension-drop theorem gives dim A_I = n+1. Finally IsLocalization.AtPrime.ringKrullDim_eq_height identifies dim A_I with height I; cancel the WithBot coercion.

proof_origin.place: Y2 fully formalized the recorded steps by finite-variable induction; local Krull intersection uses the Mathlib Jacobson specialization instead of the localization-intersection module.

mathlib_searches.query: If the associated graded ring of a maximal ideal is a polynomial ring in n variables, its height is n
If lifts of a basis of the cotangent space have no homogeneous relations in the associated graded ring of a maximal ideal, its height equals the cardinality of the basis

lean.statement: theorem height_ker_eq_card_of_homogeneous_independence {k A ι : Type*} [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [Fintype ι] (ε : A →ₐ[k] k) (x : ι → A) (hx : ∀ i, x i ∈ RingHom.ker ε) (hspan : ∀ a ∈ RingHom.ker ε, ∃ c : ι → k, a - ∑ i, algebraMap k A (c i) * x i ∈ RingHom.ker ε ^ 2) (hind : ∀ (r : ℕ) (f : MvPolynomial ι k), f.IsHomogeneous r → aeval x f ∈ RingHom.ker ε ^ (r + 1) → f = 0) : (RingHom.ker ε).height = Fintype.card ι
